item.title: Iran's president gives a rare wartime speech at the U.N.
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the U.N. General Assembly a day after President Trump threatened from the same podium to "annihilate" Iran.

item.title: It's getting harder to afford rent in the U.S., even for middle-income families
item.description: Housing affordability challenges are spreading to higher income brackets, according to new research, which found one in five renters struggled last year to pay for their housing in full and on time.

item.title: Greetings from Edinburgh, where a cheeky tour guide makes art history hilarious
item.description: For anyone who grew up staring blankly at museum artwork, this is the fun that was missing: Coco leads interactive and (mostly) factual art history comedy tours.

item.title: Is Nepal's flood a harbinger of what's to come in the Himalayas?
item.description: Building dams and hydropower plants in the Himalayas holds great promise for providing electricity. In the wake of the Nepal disaster, experts are asking about the risks of such construction.

item.title: Will FDA advisers recommend a multi-cancer blood test for approval? They'll vote
item.description: The company Grail says its Galleri blood test can detect up to 50 forms of cancer. An independent panel of experts will decide if the test should be recommended for FDA approval.

item.title: DOJ defends White House media ban, urges court to reject lawsuit
item.description: The Department of Justice defended President Trump's recent media ban, arguing that reporting by CNN, MS Now and Politico on a wide range of issues jeopardized national security and spread falsehoods.

item.title: Major news outlets banned by Trump will have their day in court
item.description: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are asking a federal judge to hold the president in check for what they say is a violation of their Constitutional rights simply because he doesn't like how they cover him.

item.title: African pop was poised for a U.S. takeover. Can its stars finish the job?
item.description: The dam appeared to break in 2024, as South African phenom Tyla made Grammy and chart history. But for a wide field of buzzed-about voices, the path to a crossover has narrowed.
